id.description: Stable slug. Never reuse or renumber.

type.description: open-response has no machine-gradable answer; it shows model reasoning after the user commits an answer. numeric-multi asks for several labelled figures at once — use it when the teaching point is decomposing a total, not arithmetic.

case_study.description: Filename in /case-studies this question draws on. Omit for standalone questions.

scenario.description: Situational setup shown before the prompt. Keep under ~200 words.

rationale.description: Why this option is right or wrong. Shown per-option after answering.

answer.description: String for multiple-choice, array for multi-select/ordering, number for numeric, null for open-response.

answer_tolerance.description: For numeric questions: acceptable absolute deviation, symmetric around answer.

answer_range.description: For numeric questions: an explicit accepted band, for cases where the defensible range is not symmetric around a point estimate. Use instead of answer_tolerance, not alongside it.

answer_unit.description: Unit for a numeric answer, shown beside the input and in feedback (e.g. "$M", "%", "FTE"). Omitting it invites unit-mismatch answers that look like reasoning errors.

parts.description: For numeric-multi: the labelled figures the user must supply. Each part is graded independently and the question is correct only when every part is; the feedback reports which parts were right.

rationale.description: Why this figure is what it is. Shown per-part after answering.

explanation.description: The teaching content. Required on every question — this is the point of the app.

community_type.description: Id from taxonomy/community-types.json — what kind of place the scenario is set in. Orthogonal to competencies: the same topic has different right answers in a legacy industrial city and a high-growth exurb. Omit only for questions that are genuinely place-independent, such as definitional ones. Validated by scripts/validate_questions.py rather than by an enum here, so adding a type is a taxonomy change.

source_tier.description: Licensing posture of the material this question is grounded in, so a change in posture is a query rather than a re-audit. public-domain: federal, state or municipal government works, whose figures and findings may be used directly. link-only: copyrighted but readable — cite by URL, write an original composite, reproduce nothing. design-reference: paid or gated material read for case architecture only, with no content drawn from it. original: invented from scratch with no external grounding. See data-sources/SOURCES.md.

data_reference.description: Optional link to a dataset backing a projection-style question.
